lines.japanese: こうして玉泉せんせいの、楽しい（願望）アルバイト講座が始まりました。
lines.english: And so began Tamaizumi's Fun (I Hope) Guide to Working Part-Time.

lines.japanese: 「それではよろしくお願いします」
lines.english: “Very well. I look forward to working with you.”

lines.japanese: 「はいっ、よろしくお願いします！」
lines.english: “Yes! Likewise!”

lines.japanese: 俺は接客サービスの鉄則「明るく元気にハッキリと」の姿勢で授業に望みました。
lines.english: I entered the lesson in full customer-service mode: bright, energetic, and crystal clear.

lines.japanese: 「えー、まず控え室のファイリングキャビネット、一番下の段に従業員向け実務マニュアルがあります」
lines.english: “First, you will find the employee operations manual in the bottom drawer of the filing cabinet in the staff room.”

lines.japanese: 「はいっ！」
lines.english: “Yes!”

lines.japanese: 「大抵のことはそれを読めば分かるので穴が開くほど精読してください」
lines.english: “Almost everything you need is in there, so study it closely enough to wear holes through the pages.”

lines.japanese: 「はいっ！」
lines.english: “Yes!”

lines.japanese: 「以上です」
lines.english: “That is all.”

lines.japanese: 「はいっ！」
lines.english: “Yes!”

lines.japanese: 「──て、えええっ、それで終わり！？」
lines.english: “—Wait, whaaat? That's the whole lesson?!”

lines.japanese: 早っ！
lines.english: That was fast!

lines.japanese: 「なにか」
lines.english: “Is there a problem?”

lines.japanese: しかも怖っ！
lines.english: And terrifying!

lines.japanese: 「え、えーと、質問してもよろしいでしょうか」
lines.english: “Um, may I ask a question?”

lines.japanese: 「どうぞ」
lines.english: “Go ahead.”

lines.japanese: 「玉泉せんせいは放任主義なんですか」
lines.english: “So, Tamaizumi, are you one of those sink-or-swim instructors?”

lines.japanese: 「はい。比較的」
lines.english: “Yes. Relatively speaking.”

lines.japanese: 「比較的！？」
lines.english: “Relatively?!”

lines.japanese: 「なにか」
lines.english: “Is there a problem?”

lines.japanese: 「え、えーっと……」
「問題ないようですね。はい。それではさっそく取りかかってください」
lines.english: “No problem, then. Good. Get started.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのう、それは俺ひとりで、ですよね？」
lines.english: “You mean... by myself?”

lines.japanese: 「私が千歳さんと肩を並べて、マニュアルに目を通す必要があると思います？」
lines.english: “Do you believe it necessary for me to stand shoulder to shoulder with you and read through the manual?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ないかもしれませんねえ」
lines.english: “Ah. Perhaps not.”

lines.japanese: 「はい。ではおひとりで。じっくりご覧になってきてください」
lines.english: “Correct. Go by yourself. Take all the time you need.”

lines.japanese: すっ。
lines.english: A graceful point.

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは微笑みながら、揃えた四本の指で一点を差しました。店の出口です。
lines.english: Smiling, Hiyoko indicated a single point with four neatly aligned fingers: the restaurant's exit.

lines.japanese: ま、たしかに外にも非常階段はありますけど、そんな、わざわざ追いだすみたいな仕草をしなくても……。
lines.english: True, the emergency stairs were outside too, but she hardly needed to gesture as if throwing me out...

lines.japanese: 「あのう……つまり、これは、いきなり窓際部署へ配属ってことですか俺」
lines.english: “Um... does this mean I've been sent straight to the corporate graveyard on my first day?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、研修期間だとお考えください」
lines.english: “No. Consider it a period of training.”

lines.japanese: 「でも自分、いちおー短期の臨時ヘルプってことでお伺いしてんすけど」
lines.english: “But I'm only supposed to be short-term temporary help.”

lines.japanese: 「すみません。どんなに忙しくても、猫の手未満は借りたところで逆効果ですから」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. However busy we may be, borrowing something less useful than a cat's paw would only make matters worse.”

lines.japanese: 「肉球にも劣る存在！？」
lines.english: “I'm less useful than a cat's paw?!”

lines.japanese: いやはや、噂どおりの厳しいひとです。
lines.english: My, my. She was every bit as strict as advertised.

lines.japanese: 「わ、分かりました」
lines.english: “U-understood.”

lines.japanese: 俺は負けじと笑顔で答えました。
lines.english: I refused to be beaten and answered with a smile.

lines.japanese: 「可及的すみやかにマニュアルを読みとげ、百獣の王となって戻ってまいります！」
lines.english: “I shall devour this manual with all possible speed and return as king of the beasts!”

lines.japanese: かくして獅子の仔はそう言いのこし、自ら千尋の谷へ向かうのでありました。
lines.english: And so the lion cub spoke, then marched of his own accord into the fathomless ravine.
THUD!

lines.japanese: 「おおおおお重たっ！」
lines.english: “Th-th-this thing is heavy!”

lines.japanese: キャビネットから引っぱりだしたその分厚いファイルは、小憎らしいウェイトレスのひとりぐらい軽く撲殺できそうなほどの重量感に溢れていました。
lines.english: The massive binder I hauled from the cabinet had enough sheer weight to bludgeon one irritating waitress with ease.

lines.japanese: 俺はそれをテーブルの上へ移すと、仕事着のドレスシャツを第二ボタンまで外して、どっかりとソファーに腰を据えました。
lines.english: I moved it to the table, unbuttoned my work shirt down through the second button, and planted myself heavily on the sofa.

lines.japanese: 横から覗くと、Ａ４のＯＡ用紙が目算でざっと……２００枚以上？
lines.english: Seen from the side, the stack looked to contain... at a rough estimate, more than two hundred sheets of A4 printer paper?

lines.japanese: うえぇぇ、予想をはるかに上回る分量です。
lines.english: Ugh. Far beyond anything I had imagined.

lines.japanese: ぱらぱらとめくってみれば、その内容は……えー、お手々の洗い方からテーブルマナーまで、やたらと幅広く多岐に渡っております。ていうか渡りすぎです。
lines.english: A quick flip revealed a prodigious range of subjects, from How to Wash Your Itty-Bitty Hands to the finer points of table manners. Far too prodigious.

lines.japanese: マニュアル至上主義の是非が問われて久しい昨今、果たして皆さんコレ、本当に全部守ってるんですかねえ……。
lines.english: In this age of endless debate over blind obedience to manuals, did everyone here truly follow every last rule...?

lines.japanese: 「あははははー」
lines.english: “Ah ha ha ha...”

lines.japanese: ぱら、ぱら、ぱらぱらぱらぱら。
lines.english: Flip. Flip. Flip-flip-flip-flip.

lines.japanese: 俺はその紙束にそよそよ吹かれながら、呆けたように笑うのでした。
lines.english: I laughed vacantly as the sheaf of paper fanned a gentle breeze across my face.

lines.japanese: ぱらぱらぱらぱら。
lines.english: Flip-flip-flip-flip.

lines.japanese: あらーコレ、実務的な作業説明だけでなく、接客やサービス精神のなんたるかまで説いておられますねー。はー、なんか本屋さんで売ってるビジネスマン向けの教養書みたいですねー。
lines.english: Well, now. Besides practical instructions, it expounded on the very nature of hospitality and the spirit of service. It read like one of those business self-help books from a bookstore.

lines.japanese: え、ていうか調理器具の使い方とか効率的な人材配置なんて、フロア担当の俺には関係ないページもいっぱいあるんですけど、こんなのまで読めとおっしゃるんですかね玉泉せんせえは……。
lines.english: And wait—there were whole sections on kitchen equipment and efficient staff allocation. None of that had anything to do with waiting tables. Did Tamaizumi, my esteemed instructor, really expect me to read even those pages...?

lines.japanese: ぱらららららぁ……。
lines.english: Frrrrrrrip...

lines.japanese: そよ風と共に流れていく、文字、文字、図解、文字、図解。
lines.english: Words, words, diagrams, words, diagrams, all streaming past on the breeze.

lines.japanese: えーまー、これは個人的な問題ですが、俺はきのう半日ずっと文字を書いたり読んだりしてたもんで、それでなくても目が疲れてるんですよね。
lines.english: This was a personal problem, admittedly, but I had spent half the day yesterday reading and writing. My eyes were already tired enough.

lines.japanese: まぶたのマッサージなんてしてみると、眼精疲労に悩まされる米田さんの姿が浮かんで、それからゆうべの電話越しの声に連鎖して……それから宮川書店で買った二冊の文庫本が思いだされました。
lines.english: When I tried massaging my eyelids, I pictured Yoneda suffering from eye strain. That led to her voice over the telephone last night, which in turn reminded me of the two paperbacks I had bought at Miyagawa Books.

lines.japanese: いまはスポーツバッグの中、というかロッカーの中に入っている細川玉木の著作。
lines.english: Tamaki Hosokawa's books were in my sports bag now—which was itself in my locker.

lines.japanese: ああ、今日はその辺のことを日和子さんといろいろ話そうなんて思ってたのに、さっきの冗談みたいなドタバタ騒ぎのせいで何にも話せなかったなあ。
lines.english: I had meant to talk with Hiyoko about all that today. Instead, the ridiculous commotion earlier had kept us from speaking at all.

lines.japanese: ああ、そうか。そうだった。
lines.english: Ah. Of course. That was it.

lines.japanese: 日和子さんがいかんせん俺に優しくないのは、なにも彼女の制服を触ってたからとか、胸を掴んじゃったからとか、そんなつまんないことじゃなくて──
lines.english: The real reason Hiyoko was being so unkind to me wasn't some trivial matter like my touching her uniform or grabbing her breasts—

lines.japanese: （いや、まあ、それもあるでしょうけど！）
lines.english: (Though, well, I'm sure that was part of it!)

lines.japanese: さかのぼって、インタビューと称してパンツの色を聞いちゃったからとか──
lines.english: Nor was it that, even earlier, I had asked what color panties she wore under the pretext of an interview—

lines.japanese: 着替え中のドアを開けちゃったからとか、そんなことでもなくて──
lines.english: Nor that I had opened the door while she was changing—

lines.japanese: （いや、もちろんそれもあるでしょうけど！）
lines.english: (Though of course that was part of it too!)

lines.japanese: （ていうか、ぜんぶ不慮の事故とはいえ、色々やりすぎだろ俺！）
lines.english: (Actually, accidents or not, I had done altogether too much!)

lines.japanese: じゃなくて──いちばん大きい要因は、俺が誉めちぎったはずの彼女の作品を、本当はまだ読んでなかったってことが知られちゃったから、なんだろうなあ。
lines.english: No. The greatest reason must have been that she had learned I had never actually read the work I had praised so lavishly.

lines.japanese: うん……面白かったって俺の言葉に、日和子さん素で喜んでたもんなあ。
lines.english: Yes... Hiyoko had been sincerely happy when I told her I enjoyed it.

lines.japanese: あの日和子さんが、無条件の笑顔でありがとうなんて言っちゃってたもんなあ。
lines.english: Hiyoko, of all people, had smiled without reservation and thanked me.

lines.japanese: ていうか、あんな風に微笑まれちゃって、俺ぶっちゃけ惚れかけたもんなあ。
lines.english: And after she smiled at me like that, I had honestly come close to falling for her.

lines.japanese: ていうか、すでに惚れてんのかもなあ。だから落ちこんでんのかもなあ。
lines.english: Maybe I had already fallen for her. Maybe that was why I felt so low.

lines.japanese: ふぅ……。
lines.english: I let out a sigh.

lines.japanese: 彼女の作品……もし読みおわったら、そのときは今度こそ本当の感想を伝えたいなあ。
lines.english: Her work... When I finished it, I wanted to tell her what I really thought this time.

lines.japanese: いや、万一それが悪い感想だったりしたら、それはまあ、そのとき考えるとして……。
lines.english: If by some chance my real opinion was unflattering, well, I could deal with that when it happened...

lines.japanese: 「やっぽーん！」
lines.english: “Yoo-hoo!”
“—Whoa!”

lines.japanese: 「うーす千歳ー、サボってんじゃねーぞー」
lines.english: “Hey, Chitose. Don't think you can sit around slacking.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっ……な、なんすかいきなり！　びっくりするなあ、もう。ノックぐらいしてくださいよ先輩方」
lines.english: “Hey! Wh-what was that for? You scared me. Shouldn't my esteemed seniors at least knock first?”

lines.japanese: 「わ、先輩だって、懐かしい響き。二年ぶりだあ」
lines.english: “Wow, ‘senior.’ Haven't heard that in ages. Two years.”

lines.japanese: 「え、予備校って先輩後輩ないの？」
lines.english: “What, cram schools don't have seniors and juniors?”

lines.japanese: 「ないよ！　あったらいじめだよ！」
lines.english: “Of course not! That'd be bullying!”

lines.japanese: 「でも、地元に帰ったら、昔の後輩とか会わなくない？」
lines.english: “But don't you run into kids from the grades below you when you go back home?”

lines.japanese: 「だって私、しばらく実家帰ってないもん」
lines.english: “I haven’t been back home for a while.”

lines.japanese: 「まじでー。じゃあ今度の暮とか、帰った方がいんじゃない」
lines.english: “Seriously? Then maybe you ought to go home over New Year's.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そのうちね」
lines.english: “Yeah. One of these days.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、紀奈子さんちの苺、また食いてー」
lines.english: “Ah, I want some more strawberries from Kinako’s family farm.”

lines.japanese: ふたりのおねえさま方は十五分間の小休憩を頂いてきたらしく、仕事着のままソファーに──つまり俺の正面に腰を下ろされました。
lines.english: Our two grande dames had apparently been granted a fifteen-minute break. Still in uniform, they sat on the sofa—directly across from me, in other words.

lines.japanese: 「千歳君ごめんねー、お邪魔しまーす」
lines.english: “Sorry, Shusuke. Mind if we join you?”

lines.japanese: 「ああいえ、お疲れさまです」
lines.english: “Not at all. You two holding up okay?”

lines.japanese: 「さんくー。でも今アイドルタイムだったから、あんまり疲れてないよー」
lines.english: “Thanks. But it's idle time right now, so we're not exactly worn out.”

lines.japanese: 「は、なんすかアイドルタイムって。フリッキー５の曲でも流す時間ですか」
lines.english: “Huh? What's idol time? The hour when you play Fricky Five songs?”

lines.japanese: 「千歳、ボケ古りぃー」
lines.english: “Chitose, that joke is ancient.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、つまんねーって言われるよりショック！」
lines.english: “Wow. Somehow that hurts worse than being told it wasn't funny!”

lines.japanese: 「アイドルタイムってゆーのは、うちの場合、お客さんがほとんど来ない時間帯のことだよ」
lines.english: “Here, ‘idle time’ means the stretch when hardly any customers come in.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、なんだ。お客さん来ないなら、遠慮なくフリッキー５流せるじゃないすか。流しましょうよ。なんだったら俺が歌ってもいいすよ。二重の意味でアイドルタイムにしましょうよ」
lines.english: “Oh, is that all? If there are no customers, we can play all the Fricky Five we like. Let's do it. I'll even sing. Then it'll be idol time in both senses.”

lines.japanese: 「……おまえ、発想が店長と同レベルだな」
lines.english: “...Your mind works on exactly the same level as the boss's.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ、何その失礼な比較。ちょっと、それどーゆーことすか。俺のどこが狩男的だって言うんですか」
lines.english: “What? What an insulting comparison. What does that mean? Which part of me is remotely Karuo-like?”

lines.japanese: 「さっき店長も言ってたんさ。自分が司会のオリジナル店内放送を流して、二重の意味でアイドルタイムにしようって」
lines.english: “The boss said the same thing earlier. He wanted to host his own in-house broadcast and make it idol time in both senses.”

lines.japanese: 「屈辱のシンクロニシティ！」
lines.english: “A humiliating synchronicity!”

lines.japanese: 「千歳君、知ってた？　うちの店長って若いころ、ラジオのパーソナリティに憧れてたらしいよ。そういえば、たしかに声はかっこいいもんね」
lines.english: “Did you know, Shusuke? Apparently our boss dreamed of being a radio host when he was young. He certainly does have a handsome voice.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ほんとに声“だけ”だけど」
lines.english: “Yeah. His voice—and only his voice.”

lines.japanese: 「え、でもいくら声が良くたって、あの歩くＮＧワード大全集にマイクなんか持たせたら、アイドルタイムどころか深夜のＡＭ放送でさえ流せなくなりますよ」
lines.english: “Even with a voice like that, if you handed that walking encyclopedia of words you can't say on air a microphone, you couldn't broadcast the results on late-night AM radio, never mind idle time.”

lines.japanese: 「だよねー。だったらまだ、私たちの歌った歌とか流した方が二重の意味でアイドルタイムだよねー」
lines.english: “Right? It would still be idol time in both senses if we played recordings of ourselves singing.”

lines.japanese: 「うえー、紀奈子さんそれイターい。とか言いつつ、ちょっと面白そう？　どうせ顔は出ないし？」
lines.english: “Ugh, Kinako, that's painfully embarrassing. Though... now you mention it, maybe it sounds kind of fun? Nobody would see our faces.”

lines.japanese: 「おお、いいじゃないすか！　それだったらフリッキー５の歌を歌えば三重の意味でアイドルタイムですよ」
lines.english: “Oh, great idea! And if we sang Fricky Five songs, it would be idol time in three senses.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、それだったら、やっぱ店長にＭＣやらせた方がいいや。うちらのイタさが薄まるから」
lines.english: “Actually, in that case, we should have the boss emcee it. He'd make us sound less embarrassing.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあさじゃあさ、今度カラオケ行って収録してこようよ。たしか店長、そういう機材持ってたよね」
lines.english: “Then let's go to karaoke sometime and record it. I'm pretty sure the boss owns the equipment.”

lines.japanese: 「おおっ、なんか本気っぽくなってきましたねえ！　それならユニット名はフリッキー５にあやかって、アレックス３にしましょう！」
lines.english: “Oh! This is starting to sound serious. Then, in homage to Fricky Five, our group shall be Alex Three!”

lines.japanese: 「ハ？　なに３って。私と紀奈子さんでアレックス２じゃん」
lines.english: “Huh? Why three? Kinako and I are Alex Two.”

lines.japanese: 「仲間といるのにロンリネス！」
lines.english: “Lonely even among friends!”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょっと！　なにそれ、なんで俺デビュー前から卒業扱いなんですか！」
lines.english: “Wait! Why have I graduated before we even debut?!”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だってバランス的におかしいじゃん。全ボーカルで男１女２ってソレ」
lines.english: “Because the balance is all wrong. One man and two women, all singing lead?”

lines.japanese: 「え、そんな、ぶっちゃけただのカラオケにバランスも何も」
lines.english: “It’s only karaoke. Does balance really matter?”

lines.japanese: 「でも男女混声ボーカルって、商業戦略的に見たら売りこむべきターゲット層が曖昧になって、最初から敗戦色濃厚だよね」
lines.english: “But in commercial terms, mixed-gender vocals blur the target demographic. The project would look doomed from the outset.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、中途半端に本格的だ！」
lines.english: “Wow. That got weirdly professional!”

lines.japanese: 「分かった、じゃあじゃあ、こうしましょうよ。俺がリードボーカルで、女性ふたりがコーラスっていう」
lines.english: “Fine, then. How about this? I sing lead and the two women provide backing vocals.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　ばっか、おまえ、私を裏に下げてどーすんだよ。この日野英里子の歌声が、かつて巷でなんと呼ばれてたか知らないのかよ」
lines.english: “What? Idiot, why would you push me into the background? Don't you know what the singing voice of Eriko Hino was once called around town?”

lines.japanese: 「え、なんて呼ばれてたんすか」
lines.english: “What was it called?”

lines.japanese: 「天使の鐘」
lines.english: “The Angel's Bell.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、さすがの紀奈子さんも呆れちゃっ──」
lines.english: “Ha ha! Even Kinako's appalled by—”

lines.japanese: 「私も！」
lines.english: “Mine too!”

lines.japanese: 「──おまえもか！」
lines.english: “You too?!”

lines.japanese: 「よーし、天使の鐘ふたつでアレックス２決まりだな」
lines.english: “Excellent. Two Angel's Bells. Alex Two it is.”

lines.japanese: 「決まってない！」
lines.english: “Nothing is official!”

lines.japanese: 「おはよー、みんなたち！　紀奈子と英里子でアレックス２だよー！」
lines.english: “Good morning, everybody! We're Alex Two, Kinako and Eriko!”

lines.japanese: 「３だよう！」
lines.english: “Three!”

lines.japanese: 「えー、じゃあ、そしたら千歳君はプロデューサーってことにしてあげるよ」
lines.english: “Fine. We’ll let you be the producer, Shusuke.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあって！　そんな、進路の決まってない子にとりあえず『家事手伝い』の肩書きを付けて事なきを得るみたいにアナタ！」
lines.english: “What do you mean, ‘fine’? You can't put ‘helps out at home’ under occupation for a kid with no plans and pretend that settles their future!”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ敏腕プロデューサーってことにしてあげるよ」
lines.english: “Fine. We’ll let you be a hotshot producer.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、じゃあって！　そんな、読者の声が届いてるはずもない新連載の第二話目にとりあえず『人気爆発！』とか付けて適当に煽っておくみたいにアナタ！」
lines.english: “There it is again! That's like slapping ‘Popularity Explodes!’ on chapter two of a new comic series before a single reader response could possibly arrive!”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ、いちいちうるせーなあ。がっつくなよ、敏腕プロデューサー」
lines.english: “God, you complain about everything. Don't be so desperate, Hotshot Producer.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、なんか早くも蔑称っぽいニュアンスになってるし！」
lines.english: “Wow. That already sounds like an insult!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ごめーん敏腕プロデューサー、ちょっとエアコンの温度下げてー」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry, Hotshot Producer. Could you turn down the air-conditioning?”

lines.japanese: 「敏腕プロデューサー、威厳ねえー！」
lines.english: “The Hotshot Producer commands no respect!”

lines.japanese: 俺はそばにあったリモコンを拾いあげ、殴るような勢いでボタンを連打しました。
lines.english: I snatched up the nearby remote and hammered the button as if trying to punch straight through it.

lines.japanese: 「うら！　うら！　凍えろ、凍えてしまえ！　ダイヤモンド・ダスト！」
lines.english: “Take that! And that! Freeze! Freeze solid! Diamond Dust!”

lines.japanese: 「ふんだ、いいですよもう。鷲介、普通の男の子に戻ってやる！　はい、アレックス３解散！　さー、もー散って散って！」
lines.english: “Hmph! Fine. Shusuke is going back to being an ordinary boy! Alex Three is disbanded! Go on, scatter! Shoo!”

lines.japanese: 「いじけんなって、敏腕プロデューサー。じゃあさ、アレックス２フィーチャリング鷲介にしてやるよ」
lines.english: “Don't sulk, Hotshot Producer. Fine, we'll call ourselves Alex Two featuring Shusuke.”

lines.japanese: 「結構です。俺、仕事中ですから邪魔しないでください。はあー、忙しい忙しい！」
lines.english: “No, thank you. I’m working, so stop distracting me. Ah, so busy! Terribly busy!”

lines.japanese: 俺は前のめりに頭を落とし、鼻が付くような距離で広げたファイルを眺めたおしました。
lines.english: I pitched my head forward and resumed glaring at the open binder from close enough for my nose to touch it.

lines.japanese: 「はー、そういえば千歳君、フロアにも厨房にも来ないで、ここで何の仕事してたの？」
lines.english: “Oh, speaking of which, Shusuke, if you haven’t gone out to the floor or the kitchen, what kind of work have you been doing in here?”

lines.japanese: 「お勉強です」
lines.english: “Studying.”

lines.japanese: ずしり。重量感あふれるファイルを立てて、ふたりに背表紙の文字をお見せしました。
lines.english: With a heavy thud, I heaved the binder upright and showed them its spine.

lines.japanese: 「従業員規則と心構え……ああ、あれだ。マニュアルだ」
lines.english: “Employee Rules and Professional Conduct... Oh, that thing. The manual.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　千歳ぇ、おま、そんなん読んでる暇あったら現場出なよ。習うより慣れろって言うだろー」
lines.english: “What? Chitose, if you've got time to read that, get out there and work. You learn by doing.”

lines.japanese: 「おっしゃる通り！」
lines.english: “Precisely!”

lines.japanese: 「だよね。まず実際に動いてみてからじゃないと、なかなかそういうの頭に入らないしね」
lines.english: “Right. It’s hard to absorb any of that until you’ve actually tried doing the work.”

lines.japanese: 「まったくもって！」
lines.english: “Quite so!”

lines.japanese: 「いや、分かってんならやめろよ」
lines.english: “Then quit reading it if you know that, idiot.”

lines.japanese: 「だって！　今日入ったばかりのぺーぺーにそんな決定権ないっすよ！」
lines.english: “But I just started today! A greenhorn like me doesn't get to make that call!”

lines.japanese: 「だから、嘘でも読んだってことにしときゃいいじゃん。うちでそんなん、まともに読んでるやついないから、どうせバレないでしょ」
lines.english: “Just lie and say you read it. Nobody here has ever read the thing properly, so who's going to catch you?”

lines.japanese: 「え、マジすか？」
lines.english: “Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 思わぬ裏技をレクチャーされ、俺は思わずファイルを閉じました。
lines.english: Having been taught this unexpected trade secret, I closed the binder without thinking.

lines.japanese: 「焦ったー。いや、英里子さんナイス助言！　実を申せばワタクシ、マニュアルがこんな分厚いと知って途方に暮れていたところだったのです。なんせ、穴開くほど読め言われてましたから」
lines.english: “What a relief. Excellent advice, Eriko! To confess the truth, I had despaired when I saw how thick this manual was. I was ordered to read it until I wore holes through the pages.”

lines.japanese: 「誰に？」
lines.english: “Who told you to?”

lines.japanese: 「トレーナーに」
lines.english: “My trainer.”

lines.japanese: 「ソレ嫌がらせじゃないの。意味ないよ、その作業」
lines.english: “That's harassment. The task is pointless.”

lines.japanese: 「これぞ世に云う囚人の穴掘り！？」
lines.english: “So this is that old prison punishment—digging a useless hole?!”

lines.japanese: 「あたたた、ぽんぽん痛くなってきた……」
lines.english: “Ow, ow, ow. My tummy suddenly hurts...”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ひどーい、千歳君の担当って誰？」
lines.english: “That’s awful. Who’s in charge of you, Shusuke?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、玉泉トレーナーですけど」
lines.english: “Coach Tamaizumi.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、たまひよかー……」
lines.english: “Ah. Tama-chick...”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ひよちゃんねー……」
lines.english: “Ah. Hiyo...”

lines.japanese: ふたりは合点がいったらしく、しみじみ首を縦に振るのでした。
lines.english: The two nodded slowly, as though everything had become clear.

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょっと、なんすかその悟りきったような反応」
lines.english: “Wait. What's with that all-knowing reaction?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ、ひよちゃんらしいなって。あはは……」
lines.english: “Well, that does sound like Hiyo. Ha ha...”

lines.japanese: 「あははじゃないっすよ、俺の身にもなってくださいよ、まったく……」
lines.english: “Don’t laugh. Try putting yourself in my position, honestly...”

lines.japanese: しかし良い情報を得たぞ。
lines.english: Still, I had acquired valuable intelligence.

lines.japanese: 読んでも意味はない、そして読まなくてもバレない──それならもう、ねえ？　これ以上めんどくさいコトはしなくても良いんじゃないでしょうか？　え、どうする？
lines.english: Reading it was pointless, and no one would catch me if I didn't. In that case, well? Surely I needn't go on with anything so tiresome. What do you think?
